content: 1. The combination of emtricitabine, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (tenofovir DF), and efavirenz is recommended as a complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years or older who weigh at least 40 kg. It should be taken as one tablet orally once daily on an empty stomach, preferably at bedtime. 2. When co-administered with rifampin in patients weighing 50 kg or more, an additional 200 mg/day of efavirenz is recommended because rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing the levels and efficacy of efavirenz. 3. This combination is not recommended for patients with moderate-to-severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <50 mL/min). 4. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be used with other antiretroviral agents. 5. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with streptozocin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated, and streptozocin should not be used with other nephrotoxic agents. 6. Adefovir and tenofovir DF increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, particularly nephrotoxicity. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 7. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum concentrations of tenofovir. Avoid such combinations. 8. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) medications, including tenofovir DF, may interfere with the manufacturing of autologous cell therapies like atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 9. Bacitracin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent use of bacitracin with other nephrotoxic drugs. 10. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels or effects of dabigatran and edoxaban by inducing P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration with potent P-gp inducers. 11. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with cyclosporine increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels or effects of nintedanib and sotorasib by inducing P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration or adjust the dosage of P-gp substrates as per prescribing information. 13. Abacavir and tenofovir DF increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor patients. 14. Acyclovir and tenofovir DF increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Acyclovir also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Amphotericin B (in various formulations) and tenofovir DF increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. These combinations may also increase tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by increasing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Atazanavir and tenofovir DF increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tenofovir DF decreases atazanavir levels, potentially reducing its antiviral activity. Ritonavir boosting may help compensate. 18. Bleomycin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Carboplatin and tenofovir DF increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination may also increase tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with NSAIDs (e.g., celecoxib, diclofenac, etodolac, fenoprofen, flurbiprofen) may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs and monitor closely. 21. Didanosine levels are increased by tenofovir DF, which reduces its elimination. This may increase the risk of pancreatitis. Adjust the didanosine dose to 250 mg/day if weight >60 kg or 200 mg/day if weight <60 kg. 22. Fenofibrate (including micronized and fenofibric acid formulations) increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Flucytosine increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicity of tenofovir DF. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and adjust the dose of tenofovir DF if necessary. 25. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of digoxin, dofetilide, and entecavir by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Elagolix increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Darolutamide, a BCRP inhibitor, increases tenofovir DF levels. Avoid co-administration or monitor closely for adverse reactions. 28. Dichlorphenamide and tenofovir DF both decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Tenofovir DF increases the toxicity of didanosine by reducing its elimination. Adjust the didanosine dose as needed to minimize the risk of pancreatitis. 30. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with iodinated contrast media increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Danicopan increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. 32. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of famciclovir by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of flurbiprofen by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of fenoprofen by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
